The energy storage operation mechanism for a circuit breaker is composed of several coordinated structural assemblies, including a side plate assembly, a connecting rod assembly, a cam assembly, an energy storage assembly, a rotating shaft assembly, and a control assembly. These components are arranged and interconnected in a manner that enables reliable energy storage, transmission, and release during operation of the circuit breaker.

A rotatable driving shaft is mounted within the side plate assembly and serves as the main supporting and driving element of the mechanism. The connecting rod assembly and the cam assembly are both installed on the driving shaft, allowing them to rotate or move in coordination with the shaft. Through this arrangement, the driving shaft can transmit motion to the connecting rod assembly and the cam assembly in a stable and efficient manner.

The energy storage assembly and the rotating shaft assembly are positioned on one side of the driving shaft, while the control assembly is positioned on the opposite side. This layout makes effective use of the space within the mechanism and helps reduce the overall size of the circuit breaker operating mechanism. By distributing the functional assemblies on different sides of the driving shaft, the mechanism achieves a more compact structure while maintaining smooth mechanical coordination.

The connecting rod assembly is connected to the rotating shaft assembly so that movement of the connecting rod assembly can be transferred to the rotating shaft assembly. In addition, the cam assembly is arranged so that it can come into contact with the energy storage assembly during rotation. When the cam assembly acts on the energy storage assembly, it pushes the energy storage assembly into an energy-storing state. The stored energy can then be used to drive the circuit breaker mechanism when required, ensuring fast and dependable operation.

The control assembly is configured to latch or engage with both the connecting rod assembly and the cam assembly. Through this latching relationship, the control assembly can regulate the movement of the connecting rod assembly and the cam assembly, thereby controlling the energy storage and release process. This coordinated engagement improves operational stability and ensures that the mechanism performs its intended actions accurately.

Overall, by integrating the connecting rod assembly, cam assembly, energy storage assembly, rotating shaft assembly, and control assembly around the driving shaft in a compact arrangement, the circuit breaker energy storage operation mechanism achieves a simplified structure, reduced space occupation, and high reliability. The mechanism is capable of storing and releasing energy efficiently while maintaining precise control over the operating sequence of the circuit breaker.

An energy storage operation mechanism for a circuit breaker is provided. The mechanism is arranged on a side plate of the circuit breaker and includes a driving shaft mounted on the side plate, a connected rod assembly, a cam assembly, an energy storage assembly, a rotating shaft assembly, and a control assembly. These components cooperate with one another to complete energy storage, locking, releasing, and operating actions of the circuit breaker.

In operation, external power or manual force drives the driving shaft to rotate. The driving shaft transmits motion to the connected rod assembly, which in turn drives the cam assembly. As the cam rotates, it acts on the energy storage assembly so that energy is gradually accumulated, for example by compressing or stretching an energy storage spring. When the energy storage assembly reaches a preset energy storage position, the control assembly locks the mechanism through a latch structure, thereby maintaining the stored energy and preventing accidental release.

When the circuit breaker needs to be closed or opened, the control assembly releases the latch according to an operating command. After release, the stored energy is quickly transferred through the cam assembly and the rotating shaft assembly, causing the operating shaft of the circuit breaker to rotate and complete the required switching action. The cam profile is designed to ensure smooth force transmission, stable movement, and reliable conversion between the energy storage state and the operating state.

The mechanism adopts a side plate-mounted driving shaft layout, which makes the overall structure compact and convenient to assemble inside the circuit breaker. The connected rod, cam, energy storage, rotating shaft, and control assemblies are arranged in a coordinated manner, reducing unnecessary transmission parts and improving mechanical efficiency. The latch-based control structure ensures that the stored energy can be reliably held and accurately released, thereby enhancing the safety and stability of the circuit breaker operation.

Compared with conventional mechanisms, this energy storage operation mechanism has the advantages of compact arrangement, reliable locking, rapid energy release, and stable action. It is suitable for use in various circuit breaker products, particularly where a dependable stored-energy operating mechanism is required. By using cam-driven energy storage and controlled latch release, the mechanism improves operational reliability, reduces structural complexity, and provides a practical solution for circuit breaker energy storage and switching control.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us refer to something specific. For example, when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book, not just any book. This simple word gives clarity and direction to a sentence.

Although “the” is short, it appears everywhere: in conversations, books, news, songs, and titles. It helps connect ideas and makes language more precise. Without it, many sentences would sound incomplete or confusing.

In a way, “the” shows how even the smallest words can have great importance. It reminds us that language is built not only from big, expressive words, but also from simple ones that quietly hold everything together.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the structure and function of an energy storage operation mechanism for a circuit breaker, mentioning the driving shaft, connecting rod, cam, energy storage, rotating shaft, and control assemblies.
counterfactuals.output:
An energy storage operation mechanism for a circuit breaker is a mechanical assembly that stores operating energy—typically in springs—and releases it rapidly to open or close the breaker contacts.

The mechanism generally includes a **driving shaft**, a **connecting rod**, a **cam**, an **energy storage assembly**, a **rotating shaft**, and **control assemblies**.

The **driving shaft** receives input power from a motor or manual operating handle. As the driving shaft rotates, it drives the **connecting rod**, which transfers motion to the **cam**. The cam converts the rotary motion into a controlled mechanical action used to charge the energy storage assembly.

The **energy storage assembly** usually includes one or more springs. During the charging process, the cam and connecting rod compress or tension the spring, storing mechanical energy. Once fully charged, the assembly is held in position by a latch or locking part of the control assembly.

The **rotating shaft** is connected to the circuit breaker’s contact operating system. When a closing or opening command is given, the **control assembly** releases the stored energy. The spring then discharges rapidly, driving the rotating shaft through the cam or linkage mechanism. Rotation of the shaft causes the breaker contacts to close or open quickly and reliably.

The **control assemblies** coordinate charging, locking, releasing, and resetting of the mechanism. They may include trip and close latches, release levers, auxiliary switches, and interlock parts. These components ensure that the energy storage mechanism operates in the correct sequence, prevents accidental operation, and allows remote or manual control.

In function, the mechanism separates slow energy accumulation from fast breaker operation. Energy can be stored gradually by the driving shaft and cam system, then released instantly through the rotating shaft to provide the high-speed action required for safe circuit breaker switching.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following technical invention idea into a formal patent-style summary: a circuit breaker mechanism with assemblies mounted around a rotatable driving shaft, where a cam drives energy storage and a control assembly latches the cam and connecting rod.
counterfactuals.output:
A circuit breaker operating mechanism is provided. The mechanism includes a rotatable driving shaft and a plurality of operating assemblies mounted about the driving shaft. The operating assemblies include an energy storage assembly, a cam assembly, a connecting rod assembly, and a control assembly.

The cam assembly is operatively coupled to the driving shaft and is configured to rotate with, or in response to rotation of, the driving shaft. During rotation, the cam assembly acts on the energy storage assembly to store operating energy, such as by compressing or tensioning a spring member. The stored energy is selectively released to actuate the connecting rod assembly, thereby driving a switching operation of the circuit breaker between open and closed states.

The control assembly is arranged to selectively latch and release at least one of the cam assembly and the connecting rod assembly. In a latched state, the control assembly retains the cam assembly and/or the connecting rod assembly in a predetermined operating position, thereby maintaining the energy storage assembly in an energy-stored condition or maintaining the circuit breaker mechanism in a selected switching state. In a released state, the control assembly permits movement of the cam assembly and the connecting rod assembly under the force of the energy storage assembly to perform an opening or closing operation.

The arrangement of the energy storage assembly, cam assembly, connecting rod assembly, and control assembly around the rotatable driving shaft provides a compact and coordinated circuit breaker mechanism in which rotation of the driving shaft stores operating energy, and controlled latching and release of the cam and connecting rod enables reliable switching actuation.
